characterList.description: A young man with brown hair, green eyes, and glasses. He is wearing a light blue shirt and is standing in a classroom.
characterList.name: Brian Bennett

content_metadata.description: An educational podcast focused on introducing the fundamental concepts of genetics, including traits, DNA, genes, and alleles.

qAndA.answer: A double helix, resembling a twisted ladder.
qAndA.question: What is the shape of the DNA molecule shown in the diagram?
How many chromosomes are there in a human cell?

qAndA.answer: A gene is a specific segment of DNA that codes for a trait, while an allele is one of the two versions of a gene present in a pair.
qAndA.question: What is the difference between a gene and an allele?

qAndA.answer: Because even if only one allele in a gene pair codes for dark hair, the individual will have dark hair. This means the dark hair allele overshadows the presence of a light hair allele.
qAndA.question: Why is dark hair considered a dominant trait?

youtube_description: Our traits are partially determined by our genes. Genes work in pairs, called alleles, and what we see is determined by the dominant allele in the pair. If there is no dominance, we see the recessive trait.
